1 How did you hear about us?
1 Edit | Results switch in the designer's top bar; the survey list's Responses column shows the count and opens Results. Analysts and viewers land on Results directly (read-only).
2 Filters are presets: status (Complete by default in Overview, All in Responses), time (All time, Today, 7 days, 30 days, Custom…), version. More filters: by answer (e.g. SOURCE = Search), language.
3 Choices: count and share per option, in the survey's order; Other shows how many typed texts and links to them. Bars, no pie charts. ⋯ menu: copy as image, show as table.
4 Rating, slider, number: average, median and the distribution; NPS: the NPS score with detractors / passives / promoters. Matrix: one stacked bar per row. Date: earliest, latest, by month.
5 Text: the latest three answers, then all of them in a list with search. Skipped = shown to the person but left empty; questions hidden by conditions do not count as skipped.

6 Responses: the shared data grid (AWK-19), loading more as you scroll on a cursor, newest first; columns = status, finished, time, language and the questions by variable name. 1 M responses stay fast.
7 Partial responses are shown in grey and can be filtered; they become complete when the person finishes. Deleting a response comes later (owner only, audited).
8 Side panel: all answers of one response in the language it was answered in; ‹ › to the next response; the grid stays in place.

9 Export: format first, Excel recommended; the export follows the codebook of each version, so renamed variables stay consistent. Every export is in the audit log. Also reachable from the survey list (⋯ → Export results).
10 The file is prepared as a background job (the same job the public API uses); small exports are ready almost at once.
Open for Dražan: Excel — write .xlsx with our own small writer (no new dependency, recommended), or use DocumentFormat.OpenXml (MIT, Microsoft / .NET Foundation, actively maintained)?
